decisions.rationale: Source and boundary PASS. The source explicitly sets registration-mark character height at 25 mm or more for MTOW 25 kg or more and 3 mm or more below 25 kg. The exact 25 kg inclusive boundary is unambiguous and is not answer-defining in the existing registration questions.

Source and distinct-exemption PASS. The source explicitly exempts aircraft registered during the pre-enforcement advance-registration period from Remote ID carriage. Existing Remote ID coverage focuses on the notified-area exemption and does not make this registration-timing exemption answer-defining.

Source and distinct-exemption PASS. The source explicitly exempts flights by the National Police Agency, prefectural police or Japan Coast Guard for security or other duties requiring particular secrecy. This is a separate explicit Remote ID exemption category with one uniquely supported answer.

Source and residual-airspace PASS. The source distinguishes the three additional limitation surfaces that may be designated at the named major and ordinance airports: conical, extended approach and outer horizontal surfaces. Q371 covers the basic three surfaces, so this item adds a different source-defined set.

Source, scope and boundary PASS. The source expressly applies the model-aircraft prohibition to aircraft under 100 g in air traffic control zones, air traffic information zones, special control airspace within control areas and related airspace. This is distinct from the existing emergency-airspace and weight-definition questions.

Source, scope and threshold PASS. Outside the outright-prohibited model-aircraft airspace, the source explicitly requires prior notification for flight at 250 m or more, and separately identifies airport surroundings and airway airspace at 150 m or more. The 260 m scenario uniquely triggers the 250 m branch.

Controlled Tier B PASS. Existing event coverage tests whether a gathering qualifies as an event; this candidate tests the later in-flight state where an unexpected event and third-party entry becomes apparent. The source requires immediate stop plus reroute, safe landing or other necessary measures regardless of prior permission, giving a distinct flight-phase and response-priority decision path.

Source-defined threshold PASS. The source explicitly states that flight over an event gathering is to be stopped at wind speed 5 m/s or more. The candidate correctly isolates the inclusive 5.0 m/s boundary and does not bundle the separate harm-mitigation-structure obligation.

Controlled Tier B PASS. The source defines third-party property damage as an accident without a minimum damage scale or monetary loss threshold. Existing accident questions cover response, civil liability or reporting destinations rather than this no-de-minimis classification boundary.

Source-defined accident boundary PASS. For collision or contact with a manned aircraft, the source requires damage to either aircraft or both, not damage to both. The one-sided-damage scenario directly tests that explicit condition and is not duplicated by existing general accident-response coverage.

Controlled Tier B PASS. The source expressly lists a recognized risk of collision or contact with an aircraft during flight as a serious incident even when no accident or damage occurs. This is a distinct reportable branch from collision-avoidance behavior and control-loss serious-incident coverage.

Controlled Tier B PASS. The source expressly lists an unmanned aircraft fire occurring during flight as a serious incident, without requiring injury or property damage. Existing battery/fire questions test technical risk rather than the legal reportability classification.

Source and record-content PASS. The source separately specifies daily-inspection record contents: date and place, inspector name and inspection result. Existing log questions identify record categories or flight-record contents, so the internal daily-inspection fields are a distinct answer-defining proposition.

Source and record-content PASS. The source separately specifies maintenance-record fields including date/place, person, and the content and reason for inspection, repair, modification or maintenance. This is distinct from flight-record contents and the general maintenance duty.

Source and norm-strength PASS. The source distinguishes the mandatory flight-plan notification for specific flights from the recommendation that non-specific flights also notify a flight plan. The candidate correctly tests the recommendation/obligation boundary and does not overstate it as a legal duty.
